pack.name: The Vault Beneath the Ascendant Court
pack.description: The shipping adventure. One room, two dormant sentinels, two pillars, and the thing the family letter was about.

commands.name: Strike — Dagger
commands.note: Finesse, so the +5 is DEX 2 + Trained 3. Agile, so MAP is −4/−8 rather than −5/−10.

commands.name: Shield
commands.hint: Shield (◆): a disc of force, +1 AC until your next turn begins.
commands.note: Player Core. The +1 is a circumstance bonus and lasts until the start of your next turn. Shield Block is not modelled — there are no reactions in this build.

commands.name: Rousing Splash
commands.hint: Rousing Splash (◆◆): a conjured wave crashes over you.
commands.note: Would also end persistent fire damage; nothing in this adventure applies it.

commands.name: Breathe Fire
commands.hint: Breathe Fire (◆◆, spends a rank-1 slot): click a direction — 15-ft cone, basic Reflex DC 17.
commands.note: Burning Hands was renamed Breathe Fire in the Remaster. Implemented under its legal name.

commands.name: Force Fang
commands.hint: Force Fang (◆, 1 Focus): click a sentinel within 30 ft — no attack roll, unerring force.
commands.note: Strictly a Magus focus spell (Secrets of Magic). Kept per the original design spec; it behaves like Magic Missile.

commands.name: Drink Healing Potion
commands.note: Interact. The potion is treated as already drawn, so drawing it does not cost a second action.

shattered-sentinel.name: Shattered Sentinel
shattered-sentinel.deathLine: {name} shatters into gravel and gold dust.
shattered-sentinel.wakeLine: Rubble shudders upright into a humanoid shape — {name} still keeps its post.
shattered-sentinel.sleepLine: {name} loses you in the dark. The rubble settles, and reknits.
shattered-sentinel.note: Creature -1 on GM Core's Building Creatures benchmarks, and Low on every line except Fortitude: HP 11, AC 13, attack +4, damage 1d6, Fort +5 high because it is masonry, Will +0 low because it does not think. 10 XP each against a solo level-1 PC. The binding constraint is not the statline, it is that a level-1 wizard has two spell slots and one focus point for the whole delve — see the note on vault-keeper.

vault-keeper.name: The Vault Keeper
vault-keeper.deathLine: The Keeper kneels, and does not rise. Gold dust settles over the casket.
vault-keeper.wakeLine: The shape beside the casket was never rubble. {name} stands, and the chamber narrows.
vault-keeper.note: The statline the two sentinels originally shipped with (17 HP, AC 14, fist +6 for 1d6+2), promoted to the boss it was always sized for: 15 XP against a solo level-1 PC, and the only fight the PC arrives at with a full spell list, because opening the gate restores them. The number was never wrong; it was pointed at the wrong fight, twice over.

startingInventoryNote: Three Minor Healing Potions, not two. A solo level-1 wizard's entire day is two spell slots and one focus point; potions are the only resource that can be bought rather than rested for, and the balance harness says the delve needs about thirteen points of them.

bequest.title: The Western Pillar — The Bequest
body: Chisel-work in pre-Absalom Kelish, gold leaf still bright in the grooves:
"I, Sarvel of the First Landing, leave what I carried up from the sea to the heir with wit enough to find it. The city above will grow fat and forgetful. Let this vault stay lean and patient."
A recess below the text is shaped like half of a two-piece seal.
bequest.logLine: You study the western pillar. Old words, older intent.

condition.title: The Eastern Pillar — The Condition
body: The same hand, generations older, the letters shakier:
"The sentinels do not guard the gold. They guard the question: will the heir read both stones before forcing the gate? Patience was ever the family's rarest coin."
The second half of the seal glows faintly as you finish reading. Somewhere ahead, stone grinds against stone.
condition.logLine: You study the eastern pillar. Old words, older intent.

area.name: The Vault Beneath the Ascendant Court

gate.sealedHint: The gate is sealed by a two-part sigil. Perhaps the pillars…
gate.sealedLog: The gate does not move. Two empty seal-recesses flank it.
gate.openNarrative: Both halves of the seal flare gold. The gate's counterweights release — the way north stands open.
gate.restoreNarrative: The seal's release washes back down the stair. Bruises fade, your prepared spells settle into place again, and the focus you spent returns.
gate.restoreNote: This is the adventure's only rest, and it is what makes two acts out of one room. Everything the sentinels cost you comes back except potions, which is the point: potions are the currency the delve is actually played in, and a player who slips past a sentinel using the wall blocks as cover arrives at the Keeper holding all three.
gate.openHint: The gate is open. The Inheritance waits beyond.

treasure.blockedHint: The Keeper's hand rests on the casket lid. It will not move while it stands.
treasure.title: The Absalom Inheritance
body: Inside the casket: a founder's deed, sealed the day the Starstone fell — title to a sliver of the Ascendant Court itself, made out to whichever heir could pass the sentinels and read the pillars true.
You are, as of this moment, minor landed gentry of Absalom. The paperwork will take decades.

defeat.title: Dying — the Vault Keeps Its Secret
body: Vesper falls at 0 HP and gains the dying 1 condition. With no ally to Administer First Aid, the ruin reclaims its silence.
Full dying and recovery-check rules are out of scope for this vignette — a rules-lawyer confession.

intro.narrative: Beneath the Ascendant Court, the family letter led you true: a vault older than the Starstone Cathedral, air thick with rock dust and patience.
intro.goal: Read both pillars to open the northern gate, then claim the Inheritance. A sentinel wakes if you stray within 30 ft of it and it can see you.
intro.hint: Click a lit tile to walk, or use the arrow keys. Approach the carved pillars to read them.
